title: Major overhaul tracking issue for the metadata exchange model and site
resolution: This repository is the overhaul. Its six workstreams map to this repository: dependencies and infrastructure (one build script, no generator chain to keep patched), schema fixes (every model bug below), documentation and site (the portal), new requirements (spatial, temporal, schema, personal and sensitive data), governance and release management (versioning, change requests, the release gate) and community (issue forms and Discussions). The tracking issue in co-cddo can be closed with a link here once the owners agree.

title: Rename the repository and references to DCAT Application Profile for the UK
resolution: A new repository, as the discussion suggested for a completely new solution: the model is no longer generated with LinkML and the site is no longer MkDocs. The old repository can be archived with a pointer here (ADR 0001). Old identifiers are kept in the crosswalk so existing records still map.

title: Title examples in alternative title don't follow the rules for titles
resolution: Examples now follow the sentence case rule they illustrate, and a check fails the build if an example title is in title case.

title: Distribution is incorrectly configured as an IRI or CURIE
resolution: A distribution can now be described in the same record or referred to by its IRI. The SHACL shape and JSON Schema both accept either.

title: The contact point definition is the same as the email definition
resolution: Contact point is now defined as the contact as a whole. Team name, contact form and team mailbox each have their own definitions. A contact form is the preferred route; a team mailbox is allowed; a named person is not.

title: Launch release management, lock the specification and start formal change management
resolution: Semantic versioning, a change request form, a public change log, a release gate that must pass, and released files as assets (JSON Schema, SHACL, JSON-LD context, codelists) rather than a source zip, as the discussion asked.

title: The OS postcodes example names the wrong publisher
resolution: The example is rebuilt from the public record and credits Ordnance Survey as publisher and creator.

title: Codelist pages don't link out to external vocabularies
resolution: The portal is generated by this repository's own script, so every concept links to its scheme and to the matching EU concept. The LinkML limitation no longer applies.

title: Add usage notes to access rights
resolution: Usage notes for each value, the difference from licence and security classification, and a rights statement for anything not open.

title: Recommend a taxonomy for theme values
resolution: The 14 data.gov.uk topics are the theme list, as the issue proposed, each with a readable identifier rather than a search address, and mapped to the EU data themes. The cross-government taxonomy can replace it when published.

title: What to do if there is no applicable licence
resolution: The "data sharing agreement required" value is restored, with a rights statement to describe the agreement.

title: What to do with assets that don't have a modified date
resolution: Last updated is recommended, not mandatory, and must never be invented. The created and release dates cover the rest.

title: Indicate whether the data includes sensitive information
resolution: A sensitive data property with a codelist (special category, criminal offence, children, commercially sensitive, security sensitive).

title: Indicate whether the data includes personal identifiable information
resolution: A personal data property, mandatory for critical data assets, with values for none, personal, pseudonymised, anonymised and not yet known.

title: Add a home page for the point of contact
resolution: The contact point takes a web address (vcard:hasURL), which is also the preferred route as a contact form.

title: Decide on a persistent identifier for the metadata model
resolution: w3id.org is proposed (https://w3id.org/dcat-ap-uk/), and every identifier in the profile already uses it. Registering the redirect is a pull request to the w3id.org repository, to be made by the owning team. Until then the identifiers do not resolve, and the portal says so.

title: Include schemas in the documentation site
resolution: JSON Schema, SHACL, JSON-LD context, LinkML, SKOS codelists, CSV and examples in Turtle and JSON-LD are all downloadable, with a DCAT description of them.

title: Enable declaration of the metadata's access control
resolution: A "who can see this record" property with four provisional levels, separate from the access rights of the data. Marked provisional: the issue asked for research with catalogue owners and information assurance, which has not been done.

title: Capture the schema of the underlying dataset
resolution: Conforms to (dct:conformsTo), as DCAT recommends and the issue proposed, with guidance by format and a link to the Tabular data standard. Mandatory for critical data assets.

title: Capture the reference data used and its resolution
resolution: A provisional "reference data used" property that links to the classification or code list (for example age bands) and its version.

title: Capture the temporal extent of the data resource
resolution: Time period covered (dct:temporal) with start and end dates, as the discussion recommended, plus time resolution and dataset series for repeated releases such as a census.

title: Capture the geospatial coverage of the data resource
resolution: Geographic coverage (dct:spatial) using, in order of preference, a GSS code or other controlled area identifier, a bounding box or a geometry, as the discussion concluded. The guidance names the "about the area" versus "located in the area" ambiguity raised in the thread, and points geospatial publishers to UK GEMINI.
